# T5b exact oracle (Z3, LinDistFlow)

Encoding in `src/p3/oracle_exact.py`: envelope bounds, LinDistFlow voltages (v = vm^2), benign limits, rule; line apparent power through a 16-gon relaxation that over-approximates both the benign set and the firing set, so UNSAT is a sound certificate for the linear model. One query per topology (336 topologies). SAT means at least one topology is SAT.

Two modes. Nominal: linear model as is (UNSAT certifies the linear model only). Robust: every AC condition is replaced by the weakest linear condition it implies under the error bounds delta in `rules/model_error_bounds_sherlock.json` (vm_pu 0.01509, loading 10.21, trafo_loading 3.744, p_from 0.5849, trafo_p_hv 0.6403). Robust UNSAT certifies the AC rule, provided the linear-to-AC error stays within delta on the envelope.

## Verdict per rule (robust mode)

| rule | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| R1 | refuted: a SAT model (nominal or robust) is a confirmed benign AC counterexample |
| R2 | certified relative to LinDistFlow with the validated error bound delta on the radial configurations only (166 meshed configurations not covered (LinDistFlow is radial only); those rely on the search layer) |
| R3 | inconclusive in the exact layer: robust SAT, but no SAT model is an AC counterexample; rely on the search layer |

## R3 in the exact layer

R3 is syntactically expressible (all its measurements are linear: transformer P, load P, DER P). But LinDistFlow is lossless: the transformer power equals the sum of downstream net load exactly, so the R3 residual d is identically 0 in the linear model and R3 can never fire there. Its UNSAT is therefore vacuous: it certifies nothing about R3 on the real grid, where d equals the network losses. In robust mode the transformer power error bound enters R3 as slack (two transformers), which is larger than the margin unless losses are bounded more tightly; the robust verdict above says what happens. A loss-aware layer (for example loss bounds or a convex relaxation) is needed to certify balance rules.
